title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff and regional failover under thrashing
author: Aisha Patel
body: Summary: Fixes sporadic thrashing in the SLO enforcer that caused repeated regional circuit-breaker flips and aggressive load-shedding during short-lived latency spikes. This hotfix tightens backoff ordering, introduces debounce windows on per-region cb state transitions, and smooths token-bucket accounting to avoid oscillation when multiple regions report intermittent errors. Motivation: In the last incident (see ENG-2045) we observed the enforcer rapidly tripping regional circuit breakers when upstreams reported transient latency increases, which cascaded into global routing adjustments and higher tail latency for some customers. This change reduces false positives and stabilizes failover decisions while preserving fast reaction to genuine degradation. Checklist: - [x] Reproduce thrashing pattern in perf-canary harness - [x] Implement debounce + ordering fixes - [x] Add per-region token-bucket smoothing and hysteresis - [x] Add unit + integration tests covering race conditions - [x] Roll out to canary region and monitor metrics - [x] Post-mortem and release notes Changes: - Fix race in SLO enforcer backoff queue ordering to ensure older backoff requests are respected before newer ones. - Add debounce window (configurable, default 10s) on circuit-breaker OPEN->CLOSED transitions per-region to prevent flip-flop. - Smooth token-bucket refill/shrink to use EMA over 30s to avoid sudden drops when multiple worker nodes transiently report errors. - Tighten threshold evaluation to require sustained breach for 3 consecutive evaluation windows before triggering regional failover. - Add new metrics: slo_enforcer.debounce_events, slo_enforcer.ema_fill_ratio, slo_enforcer.transition_count (tags: region, model). - Add integration test that simulates flapping upstreams and validates no more than one failover per 60s per region. Related work: Linear ENG-2045, ENG-2089; Incident INT-549. Deployment notes: Canary deployed to eu-west-1 for 2 hours then rolled to us-west-2. Monitoring dashboards updated and alerts relaxed transiently to avoid noise. Merge method: squash
commits: 1) Fix ordering bug in backoff queue and add tests 2) Implement per-region debounce and EMA smoothing 3) Add metrics and integration test harness changes 4) Update docs/observability dashboard entries 5) Bump config defaults and add migration note
release_notes: Hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover and load-shedding. Reduces false-positive circuit-breaker flips under transient upstream latency by adding debounce windows, smoothing token-bucket accounting, and tightening threshold evaluation. Metrics: slo_enforcer.debounce_events, slo_enforcer.ema_fill_ratio, slo_enforcer.transition_count.
reviews_conversation: Diego Romero (reviewer): Confirmed race condition in backoff queue; suggested preserving insertion order when timestamps are equal. Author: implemented stable ordering and added test.
Lina Chen (reviewer): Asked for observability hooks to validate debounce behavior in production. Author: added metrics and dashboard change.
Jordan Matthews (approver): Verified canary logs and metrics in eu-west-1; approved with no further changes.
SRE on-call (comment): After deploying canary we saw one false-open event in eu-west-1 during a noisy GC window; debounce prevented global failover. Recommended 24h monitoring before wide rollout.
Author (Aisha Patel): Addressed comments and bumped default debounce to 10s; added integration test for flapping upstreams.
